Two points off: one Urdu noun serves the English's 'pools' and 'lakes' (the Arabic has one), and 'lovely' is said by the Arabic's 'favourite' (round 1).

nativeness.why: Reads plainly, and «مجموعہ» is back for the 'cluster' both readers found odd. Charged: the name, which neither reader can read — the second sees a rendering of 'dolphin' and a doubled letter that looks like a slip (the Arabic's spelling, letter for letter; no ruling licenses a lighter one); the office ring of the reservation («معتبر ذرائع سے تصدیق», both readers; the source's words); «بارشوں کے دنوں میں», which to the second reader first means the monsoon (the source names no season); a plural relative after a singular head in faq[0].a (grammatical by sense). One point lower than round 1: the name is a failure of two readers, not of one.

compliance.why: Letterforms clean; title equal to its key with article and both waws; the neighbour's name one form four times; shared row and answer byte-identical with hubail-lake's. One point off: both lake names pending.

fit.why: One point off: the reader cannot say the name of the place aloud or ask the way to it. No months for the rains, no access, a lake in the title and several in the text, a favourite spot without confirmed details, a summary that says flatly what the body says of rainy days only: the source's, logged, not charged.

fields.title: جھیل الدیلفوون
fields.summary: جھیل الحبیل کے قریب چھوٹی چھوٹی موسمی جھیلیں، جو بارشوں کے دنوں میں بنتی ہیں۔ صحرا کی سیر کے لیے یہ ایک پسندیدہ مقام ہے۔
fields.body: الدیلفوون چھوٹی چھوٹی موسمی جھیلوں کا ایک مجموعہ ہے، جو الاحساء کے شمال میں جھیل الحبیل کے قریب ہے۔ یہ جھیلیں اس وقت بنتی ہیں جب بارش کا پانی نشیبی زمین میں جمع ہو جاتا ہے۔ بارشوں کے دنوں میں یہ صحرا کی سیر اور تفریح کے لیے ایک پسندیدہ مقام بن جاتی ہیں۔ مزید تفصیلات کی معتبر ذرائع سے تصدیق ابھی باقی ہے۔
fields.area: جھیل الحبیل کے قریب، الاحساء کے شمال میں

faq.a: نہیں۔ یہ چھوٹی چھوٹی موسمی جھیلوں کا ایک مجموعہ ہے، جو بارشوں کے دنوں میں بنتی ہیں، جب پانی نشیبی زمین میں جمع ہو جاتا ہے۔
جھیل الحبیل کے قریب، الاحساء کے شمال میں۔

faq.a: نہیں۔ یہ ایک کھلا عوامی قدرتی مقام ہے جہاں کوئی فیس نہیں۔

blind_reader_rulings.reason: «محفوظ» in three jobs; moderate now, where the first reader graded it minor. (1) «یہ مقام محفوظ کریں» is approved interface text of b0-ui, on every page, and is not a leaf of this batch. (2) «محفوظ قدرتی علاقہ» stands once, inside the 2019 announcement; no other native wording for a reserve is attested. (3) Booking, «جگہ آن لائن محفوظ کرائی جاتی ہے»: he stopped to work it out. The loan he offers was held to ruling P16-test again (item N90): a headword it has; a reader has now stumbled; but condition 1 is not shown — «محفوظ کرانا» is standard written Urdu for reserving a place, and the press page read in this round, which writes the loan, does not show otherwise. The native verb stays; the loan is on record for the owner in one line. Charged under nativeness on asfar and uqair-beach.

An interface string, not a leaf of this batch: trails.partOf «ان راستوں میں شامل», approved in b0-ui, where «راستہ» was ruled the word for a trail. Both readers of this batch read it as 'roads' and could not tell what is included in what; the heading stands above trail cards that are still English on /ur/. Recorded for the next interface round and the owner, now on two readers, with his wording («یہ مقام ان سیر کے راستوں میں شامل ہے»).

The labels and the wordings are the sources': 'Fees: No fee — open natural site' (asfar), 'Hours & entry' + 'Hours' + 'Fees' (salwa-beach, three approved pairs of the translation memory that may not be reworded), 'Visiting: Open public natural site — no fee' (the two lakes), and no fee row on two pages. The batch's own rows already share one wording for 'no fee' and one word for 'open' and differ only where their English differs. That «سیر» 'tells me nothing about what the row holds' is said by both readers: the English label 'Visiting' tells no more (item N86). Logged for the owner: one label and one wording for a free open site.

«کھلا» is the sources' 'open' ('open natural site', 'Open public site', «مفتوح»): whether open at all hours, to everyone, or in the open air is not said by any of the four pages but salwa-beach, which has an Hours row. The Urdu has one word for the one word and supplies no hours. Logged with the cards.
An interface string, not a leaf of this batch: the lead of the nearby strip, approved in b0-ui. Minor and understood. Recorded for the next interface round with his wording.
An interface string, not a leaf of this batch: the note on distances, approved in b0-ui. Minor and understood on a second look. Recorded for the next interface round with his wording.

«آبی اجسام» stays, and the two readers are set side by side (item N93). The first reader read «آبی ذخائر» and pictured a man-made tank behind a dam: a wrong picture, on the owner's guarded claim (build check C31). The second read «آبی اجسام», understood it as water bodies, and found it word for word and textbook. One wording misleads and the other stumbles; the one that does not mislead stays. His own wording, «… پانی کے سب سے بڑے ذخیروں میں سے ایک», is the noun that misled the first reader (candidate C of N93) and is not taken; 'lakes' is what the guard forbids. No third wording was found that keeps the three guarded points, and none is coined. Charged under nativeness and fit on asfar; both remedies on record for the owner.

The line is the template's: the approved interface string det.unesco followed by the component number of the property (1563-012), with no label, on every component page in every language. Not a leaf of the batch. Two readers now took the bare number for a year range, a phone extension or a postal code. Logged for the owner.

Both sources have the two sentences as they stand and they are the owner's wording (build check C37: a stopover, twice a year): 'pass through twice a year', then 'Migratory birds stay here from the onset of winter until May', the noun repeated. Stage 4 took out the demonstrative that had made them the same birds. Both readers ask in which months they would see birds: the source does not say, and best time gives an hour of the day only. Nothing is supplied.

«بنانے کا اعلان کیا» says an announcement because the source says one — 'announced its conversion into a nature reserve' — and the owner guards exactly that (build check C37: the announcement of 2019, not a present status). Whether it is a reserve today, and whether visitors may walk in freely, the source does not say; that the card calls it an open site beside this is the source's. He made no remark on the ministry's name: the misreading of the first reader did not recur (item N98).

The chain is the guarded fact in the line's own nouns: north-east of the PALM GROVES of the oasis, never 'north-east of the oasis' (build check C37). His wording, «نخلستان کے شمال مشرق میں», drops the groves and is what the guard forbids. The one smaller change that keeps both nouns — «… باغات سے شمال مشرق میں» — was weighed and refused: it says 'outside, to the north-east from', where both sources leave open whether the lake lies at the groves' north-east edge or beyond it (the standard of item N88). Both readers had to unpick the chain and both note that «نخلستان» already says date gardens: the cost of the termbase's word for the oasis, on record since the calibration, charged under nativeness and fit on asfar. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line: if he accepts that in Urdu «نخلستان» alone names the palm groves, the line is «نخلستان کے شمال مشرق میں». That no town or distance is given is the source's.

He read the cell as round 1 meant it — four-wheel drive only — and calls it 'the fact that decides whether my family can go at all' (confirmed again in his item 36). His remark is that the fact stands in one short card row: the body and the four questions never mention it, and nothing says how far the track is, where an ordinary car stops, or what is at the lake. All of that is the source's, in both languages. Nothing is moved from the card into the body. Logged, first among asfar's defects.

Two wordings because the sources have two: 'photographers' («المصوّرين») on asfar and 'photography enthusiasts' («هواة التصوير») on uqair-beach. The word he would say is refused by the owner's own decision (ruling P16); that every reader so far says it is on record there.

Applied: «“گوگل میپس پر دیکھیں” کا لنک کھولیں» (change 0), the wording round 1 kept on record for this outcome. Two readers said one does not 'press' a link; his own verb is a loan with no entry, and the noun now written is a loan the line has admitted. That the answer gives an instruction after the position is the source's sentence.

«مہاجر پرندے» is a verified termbase entry (21 reference pages, on lake articles, against 5 for «ہجرت کرنے والے پرندے») and is not overruled on taste. The repetition is the sources': stage 4 restored the bare noun where stage 2 had written «یہ پرندے», because the demonstrative made the birds of the two sentences the same birds, which neither source says. Minor; charged lightly under nativeness.

Applied to the clause: «خلیج کے کنارے کنارے العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر پھیلا ہوا ہے» (change 3) — both readers read it twice with «ساحل» in it twice. THE SOURCE'S, logged: 'historic' of a beach that only the port in the next sentence explains («شاطئ العقير التاريخي»).

Applied in summary and body, one string: «گرمیاں گزارنے کے سب سے پرانے مقامات» (changes 1 and 2). The superlative is in both sources and stays, with 'among'; the word he says belongs to ruins is replaced by the everyday one. THE SOURCE'S, logged: 'summer destinations' on a Gulf beach beside a card that says to keep away from the peak heat, and a body that repeats the summary's claim word for word.

Read with care, because round 1 made this reader the test: 'if he does not know what it is, the case goes to the owner … not to a third coinage'. He did not know the term — the bare label stopped him ('house-like vehicles?') — and he understood the thing only from the row's own description; 'nobody I know would call them this'. That is not the misreading the first description produced (a resident's car), and it is not a wording that reads as Urdu. So, as round 1 ruled: no third coinage; «گھر نما گاڑی» stands in the four leaves, and what the vehicle is to be called goes to the owner as item N100-caravan-loan-or-description, with both readers' loans («کیمپر وین», «کارواں»; his «کارواں (رہائشی گاڑیاں)» puts a bracket in a label and revives the description the first reader misread) and the press page read in this round, where the Gulf's Urdu paper writes «کارواں» of the unit one camps in. Charged on uqair-beach under nativeness, compliance and fit.

uqair-beach has no fee row and no hours row in either language, and says nothing on swimming or on whether the water is safe for children; its one card row is the caravan site. No row is written from another page. Logged for the owner, on two readers.
'Booked online' («يُحجز إلكترونياً») with no site, application, link or name, and no word on a charge, in both languages. Nothing is supplied.

His three doubts are the source's three words, as the first reader's were: 'adjoins' («يجاور») — beside it, so not on it?; 'set aside for visitors' («مخصّصة للزوّار») — for them only?; 'facilities' — which? The Urdu has «برابر میں», «مخصوص» and «سہولتیں», each the plain equivalent. Nothing is named that the source does not name.

The circle is in both sources: 'Where is Al-Uqair Beach? — On the Al-Uqair coast east of Al-Ahsa, beside the historic Al-Uqair port', and the area line 'Al-Uqair coast — east of Al-Ahsa'. No distance or driving time in either language. Nothing is supplied.

No vowel sign and no pronunciation gloss is added to a name: ruling P17 ('the name as written is said as the Arab says it'). Minor. That an Urdu reader cannot tell the first vowel of «العقیر» or «الحبیل» is recorded in the entries, as it was for the names of earlier batches.

The answer repeats the body's sentence because the source's answer does ('Yes. The beach suits families and photography enthusiasts, and adjoins …'), and the order of the questions is the source's. Minor. Logged.

The title is ruled (item N84: the town's key, the possessive, the generic) and the town's name keeps the form of ruling N82. That «سلویٰ» is first a woman's name to an Urdu reader is on record in the entry since b5; here the summary cleared it up for him at once. His sentence adds the generic at a mention where both sources have the name bare (the fence of rulings N61, N73 and N77) and replaces 'falls under' by 'is included in'. The sentence itself is reordered for another reason (change 4): the subject now stands first.

Hofuf is named bare in both sources at its one mention ('about 150 kilometres from Hofuf'), and it is the only distance on the six pages. The line does not complete a generic that both sources of a field leave out (rulings N61, N73, N77). Two readers now say they cannot use the distance: «ہفوف شہر سے» is on record for the owner as one line.

Minor and understood. The gateway is the image of both sources ('the Kingdom's land gateway to Qatar', «بوابة المملكة البرية إلى قطر»); a plain 'border crossing' is a fact they do not state in those words. He made no remark on the country's name, which round 1 wrote for «مملکت»: confirmed (item N91).

The sentence is the source's ('Salwa falls administratively under Al-Ahsa governorate'), and after a first sentence that sets Salwa at Al-Ahsa's far end it tells a family little in any language. Minor. It is kept, without the generic (item N92), and reordered so that the two names no longer touch (change 4, the proof's finding 1). He did not misread a word in it.

Applied to the double hedge: «کہتے ہیں کہ» is taken out and «… ریت میں شمار ہوتی ہے» alone carries 'are described as among' (change 5). His own sentence makes the superlative absolute («خوبصورت ترین ریت ہے»): the sources say 'among', and that is kept (ruling P19). On the singular «ریت» with 'reckoned among': it is the idiom of a mass noun, and the first reader offered it himself; left. That nobody is named who says so is the source's.
'Its park' («حديقته») appears in both sources with no earlier mention of a park or garden. Two readers went back to look for it. Nothing is supplied; logged.

Three minor points. «ترقیاتی کام کیے ہیں» is municipal wording said of a municipality's works; the wording before it («ترقی دی ہے») was translated-sounding to the first reader (moderate), so the lighter of the two remarks stays. «کھیل کے میدان» is as open as the sources ('playgrounds', «ملاعب»), which do not say for whom: logged. «ورزش کے آلات» is the plain native phrase; his «مشینیں» is a loan with no entry in the termbase.

Three rows saying two things in both languages; in the Urdu they are the approved pairs of the translation memory, byte for byte, with the masculine string of ruling N65 (item N87), and may not be reworded. Logged for the owner on the five pages of b5 and here: one row for hours and one for the fee would do.

Minor. A desert, like a town, takes its Urdu generic after the name («الجافورہ صحرا», the entry; ruling N73's order); the form he offers carries a Persian izafat, which the line does not write on a name (ruling P8). He did not read «مغربی جانب» as the prayer time: round 1's edit is confirmed. The proof's «مغربی جانب سے» stays on record.

The opening is the source's own: 'Al-Hubail Lake is a body of water north of Al-Ahsa', «بحيرة الحبيل مسطح مائي يقع شمال الأحساء». His sentence drops the predicate. Two renderings of it have now each failed one reader — «آبی ذخیرہ» was a dam's reservoir to the first, «پانی کا ایک پھیلاؤ» is a definition of a lake as water to the second — and still a predicate of the field's source is not dropped for register, whatever the number of readers (ruling P24). ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line: the reader's own sentence, «جھیل الحبیل الاحساء کے شمال میں ہے۔», if he accepts the opening without 'a body of water' (ruling N64 would then ask for a comma after the title or for the place first). Charged under nativeness on hubail-lake.

«زرعی نکاسی کا پانی» is the source's term, 'agricultural drainage water' («مياه الصرف الزراعي»), and that 'agricultural' is said after 'farms' is the source's too. His paraphrase adds 'surplus'. Dropping «زرعی» was weighed and refused: «نکاسی کا پانی» alone reads as sewage (the judge's own reading of the phrase, not an attestation). The two nouns for the land are two source nouns, «مزارع» here and «نخيل» on asfar (ruling N5). Both readers find it technical: charged under nativeness on hubail-lake.

SERIOUS, and wholly the source's; looked through for wording and none found. The page is two English sentences and one Arabic one — how the lake formed, and that it is north of Al-Ahsa — and the English itself ends by saying that extent and facilities are unconfirmed. What one sees or does, the water of a lake of farm run-off, the road, the vehicle: in neither language. The row that calls it an 'open public natural site' is the source's row, marked verified. A translation cannot fill it and does not. No point is taken from fit for it. FIRST among the batch's defects for the owner, now on two readers who would not take a family there.

Applied to the tail: the two things that are unconfirmed follow the closed clause after a colon (change 6); inside the clause they lost the first reader. The office ring he hears in «معتبر ذرائع سے تصدیق ابھی باقی ہے» is the source's 'pending confirmation from reliable sources', which both readers have now named in two wordings of the predicate; his own sentence drops 'further details' and 'reliable sources' — how the site states a reservation of its own is the owner's (ruling P25). Recorded as his option under item N99.

'North of Al-Ahsa' is all that either source says of the place, three times: summary, area line and the answer to 'Where is …?'. Nothing is supplied; where the lakes lie is the owner's decision (item N88).

SERIOUS, and wholly the source's and the template's; looked through for wording and none found. Summary and body are one sentence in both languages, so the page says it twice; the source has no area field, no fee row and no other text; the fountain stands only in a bracket of the Hours row. The Urdu sentence itself he read without a remark. No point is taken from fit. For the owner: a body text, an area line, a fee row, an hour for the fountain.

What makes the park 'environmental' is said in neither language; the adjective is in its name and in its one sentence. That «تفریح گاہ» is vaguer than the loan is the cost of ruling N69 (one native noun for a park), which is not reopened. Nothing is supplied.

No fee row and no area field in the source; the notice is the approved interface string det.hoursNotice, printed on every page that shows hours and not on a page flagged as an open site, and it names fees whether or not the card has a fee row; no way to reach the management is in the page's data in any language. Logged, on two readers.

Applied: «(فوارے کی نمائش غروب آفتاب کے بعد)» (change 7). Both readers read a protest first. His own remedy is the loan, which ruling P16-test still does not admit here (condition 1 is not shown: no page was obtained that writes the loan of a fountain). THE SOURCE'S, logged: whether the show is daily and at what hour — 'after sunset' until midnight is all either language says.

Minor. None of the three is a leaf of this batch. The breadcrumb and the back link are the two interface strings ruled under N96 and N97 (the two nouns of the menu label); the small label «تفریح گاہیں اور باغات» is the category name the template prints above the title (where its Urdu is kept was not traced in this round: it is not in the ur block of ui.ts under that wording). That one page names its section two ways, and files a park under bazaars, is the site's structure in every language. Recorded for the next interface round.
Minor. «عبد اللہ» in two words is ruling N27; the joined form is recorded for search in the entry. Two readers noticed and neither was stopped.

The form stays, and the rulings that build a name were read again for a lighter spelling: none is licensed. Ruling P1 writes a place name as the Arabic writes it, with its article; ruling P11 touches only the hamza on alif; ruling P17 adds no vowel sign and no gloss for pronunciation. The Arabic «الديلفوون» has two waws and the Urdu has them. Both readers failed on it — the first saw a typing slip, the second a rendering of 'dolphin'. Charged under nativeness and fit on delfoon-lake. FOR THE OWNER, as a naming question: whether the Arabic spelling with two waws is the intended one, and how the name is said.

One lake in the title and the three questions, several in the summary, the body and the first answer — in both languages (item N95); and the summary's own turn from the plural to 'a favourite spot' is the English's and the Arabic's («وجهة محببة»). Each field follows its own source.

No months and no season for the rains in either language, and no best-time field. «بارشوں کے دنوں میں» is 'in the rainy spells' («في فترات الأمطار»); that the phrase first means the monsoon to a reader from Pakistan cannot be cured without naming a season the source does not name. Logged for the owner with the access defect: he could drive out and find dry ground.

'Further details are pending confirmation from reliable sources' names nothing on this page: the source's sentence. The wording is item N99's, letter for letter hubail-lake's fixed part. No access row in either language, on a page that speaks of desert outings: logged.
Applied with his own word, which is stage 1's: «جھیلوں کا ایک مجموعہ» in the body and the first answer (changes 8 and 9).
The summary says 'a favourite spot for desert outings' flatly and the body says it of the wet spells, in both languages. Minor. Each field follows its own source (item N95).

proof_rulings.reason: Applied as the finding words it: «سلویٰ انتظامی طور پر الاحساء کے تحت آتا ہے۔» (change 4). Item N92, the entry that records the form for search and the reader ruling quote the sentence in this order.

The cell does not move; the RECORD is cured. Not fetched again in this round: the press page and the five reference pages of round 1.

No string moves; the RECORD is cured as the finding asks. The item is split. Kept, on the blind read the finding left it to. The second reader read the cell as four-wheel drive only and made it the fact his outing turns on (his items 12 and 36); nobody read the middle word as the sea animal. What he misses is the source's: the condition stands in one card row.

Kept, on the two readers set side by side (item N93; reader ruling 7). The cost is charged; the reader's own remedies are on record for the owner.

Kept. The second reader read the sentence without «اب» and made no remark. The finding's account stands: 'has become' is not said, and the sentence is a shade wider than its source; counted under accuracy on asfar.

The string stands; the RECORD is cured. The second reader made no remark on the ministry's name, so the first reader's misreading did not recur.
